title: Butterfly, Crab and Trading
lessons/harmonics-u3-l1/steps/0/body: The **Butterfly** is an **extension** pattern: B is deep (**78.6% of XA**), and D goes past X, ending at **127 to 161.8 percent** of XA. So in a bullish Butterfly, D is **below X**.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l1/steps/1/body: In a Butterfly, the CD leg is **longer than AB** and goes past X. The most common level for D is the **127% XA** extension; many traders accept up to **161.8%** too.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l1/steps/2/prompt: We have a bullish Butterfly on EUR/USD. If D is at the 127% XA extension, where is it?
lessons/harmonics-u3-l1/steps/2/explanat: 1.27 × 200 pips ≈ 254 pips from A: 1.1000 − 0.0254 = 1.0746, about 54 pips below X. (1.0676 is the 161.8% level.)
lessons/harmonics-u3-l1/steps/3/statemen: In a bullish Butterfly, point D forms below X.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l1/steps/3/explanat: A Butterfly's D is at the 127 to 161.8 percent extension of XA, beyond X. That's its main difference from the Gartley and the Bat.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l1/steps/4/prompt: B formed at 78.6% of XA and D at the 127% XA extension. Which pattern is this?
lessons/harmonics-u3-l1/steps/4/explanat: A deep B at 78.6% and a D beyond X at 127% of XA are the Butterfly's signature. In the Gartley and the Bat, D stays inside the XA leg.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l1/steps/5/title: Why does D go past X?
lessons/harmonics-u3-l1/steps/5/body: In a Butterfly, price makes a **new low below X**; many traders see this as a sweep of the stop losses below X, after which the reversal begins. That's why the Butterfly's stop loss **doesn't go beyond X**, but just **beyond the PRZ**.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l1/steps/5/tip: If price blows through the 161.8% XA level too, the Butterfly idea gets much weaker.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l1/steps/6/prompt: This is a bullish Butterfly. Tap the candle that formed D at the 127% XA extension.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l1/steps/6/explanat: This candle reached 127% of XA (56,368) with a long lower wick and closed higher. That's D, below X (58,000), and price bounced up after it.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l1/steps/7/sentence: In a Butterfly, B forms at ___ of XA and D at the ___ extension of XA.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l1/steps/7/explanat: A deep B (78.6%) and a D beyond X (127 to 161.8 percent) are the Butterfly's two main rules.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l1/steps/8/prompt: Bearish Butterfly: D has completed above X at 127% of XA with a shooting star. What's your call?
lessons/harmonics-u3-l1/steps/8/explanat: D sits at the 127% XA extension, above X, and the shooting star shows buyers weakening. A drop is more likely. Stop loss just above the PRZ, not above X, which already broke.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l2/steps/0/body: The **Crab** is another extension pattern introduced by Scott Carney, but its D is the furthest of all: **161.8% of XA**. Its B is also shallower than the Butterfly's (**38.2 to 61.8 percent** of XA).
lessons/harmonics-u3-l2/steps/1/body: In a Crab, the CD leg is **very long**, and its BC projection is the biggest of all the patterns. Its most important number is **1.618 XA** for point D.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l2/steps/2/prompt: B formed at 50% of XA and D at 161.8% of XA. Which pattern is this?
lessons/harmonics-u3-l2/steps/2/explanat: D at 161.8% of XA means an extension pattern with a very distant D, and a shallow B (50%) fits the Crab. In a Butterfly, B sits at 78.6%.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l2/steps/3/prompt: We have a bullish Crab on GBP/USD. Where's point D (161.8% of XA)?
lessons/harmonics-u3-l2/steps/3/explanat: 1.618 × 200 pips ≈ 324 pips from A: 1.2800 − 0.0324 = 1.2476, which is 124 pips below X. (1.2546 is the Butterfly's 127% level.)
lessons/harmonics-u3-l2/steps/4/body: Because a Crab's D is so far past X, the CD leg is usually **long and sharp**. Blindly stepping in front of a sharp move is risky; many traders either wait for a **confirmation candle** or enter with a **smaller position**.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l2/steps/4/tip: Put the Crab's stop loss just beyond the PRZ; X broke a long time ago.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l2/steps/5/statemen: In a Crab, point B must be at 78.6% of XA.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l2/steps/5/explanat: B at 78.6% belongs to the Butterfly. A Crab's B is shallower, between 38.2 and 61.8 percent of XA.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l2/steps/7/prompt: This is a bearish Crab. Tap the candle that formed D at 161.8% of XA.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l2/steps/7/explanat: This candle's upper wick reached 161.8% of XA (69,708) and closed much lower. That's D, well above X (66,000).
lessons/harmonics-u3-l2/steps/8/prompt: A bullish Crab has completed at 161.8% of XA, and a hammer sits in the PRZ. What's your call?
lessons/harmonics-u3-l2/steps/8/explanat: D sits at 161.8% of XA (2238.2), and the hammer shows sellers running out of steam after a sharp leg. A move back up is more likely. Stop loss just below the PRZ.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/title: Entry, Stop Loss and Target in Harmonics
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/0/body: **Aggressive entry**: a limit order inside the PRZ, entering without waiting; a better price but a higher chance of failure. **Conservative entry**: wait for a **reversal candle** or a break of a small structure; later, but with confirmation.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/0/tip: Whichever method you pick, set your stop loss and position size before you enter.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/1/title: Where does the stop loss go?
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/1/body: In the **Gartley and Bat**, where D is inside XA, the stop loss usually goes just **beyond X**, because passing X invalidates the pattern. In the **Butterfly and Crab**, X has already broken, so the stop loss goes just **beyond the PRZ** (past D).
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/2/prompt: A bullish Bat on EUR/USD has completed at D (X = 1.0800). For a buy, put your stop loss where it usually goes.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/2/explanat: In the Bat and Gartley, D is inside the XA leg and passing X invalidates the pattern, so the stop loss goes just below X (1.0800), say 1.0790. D sits at 88.6% of XA (around 1.0811); if you enter right there, the risk is only about 20 pips.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/3/prompt: Where's a sensible stop loss for a bullish Butterfly?
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/3/options/: Just below the PRZ (lower than D)
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/3/explanat: In a bullish Butterfly, D itself is below X, so "below X" is above your entry! The sensible spot is just below the PRZ.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/4/title: Take profit: Fibs of the AD leg
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/4/body: Many harmonic traders set their targets on **retracements of the AD leg**: the first target at **38.2%** and the second at **61.8%** of AD. Point C is a common target too.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/5/prompt: Bullish Bat on GBP/USD: entry at D, stop loss 10 pips below X, and the first target at 38.2% of AD. What's the approximate risk-to-reward ratio?
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/6/prompt: Put a harmonic trade in order, from start to finish.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/6/items/2: Wait for a confirmation candle inside the PRZ
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/6/items/3: Enter and set your stop loss
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/6/items/4: Close part of the position at 38.2% of AD
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/6/items/5: Move your stop loss to entry
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/6/explanat: First the pattern and the zone, then confirmation and an entry with a stop loss. When the first target hits, you close part and ride the rest risk-free.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/7/statemen: After reaching the first target, many traders close part of the trade and move their stop loss to entry.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/7/explanat: That way some profit is locked in, and if price turns back, the rest of the trade closes at roughly no loss (aside from slippage).
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/8/prompt: This is the trade plan for a bullish Gartley. Beyond which point is the stop loss placed?
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/8/explanat: The stop loss (1.0690) is just below X (1.0700), because in a Gartley, passing X means the pattern is invalid. The targets sit at 38.2% and 61.8% of the AD leg.
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/9/prompt: Wrap-up: a bearish Crab has completed at 161.8% of XA with a shooting star in the PRZ. Which trade fits this setup?
lessons/harmonics-u3-l3/steps/9/explanat: B at 61.8% and D at 161.8% of XA confirm a bearish Crab, and the reversal candle in the PRZ signals buyer weakness. Sell with a stop loss just above the PRZ and the first target at 38.2% of AD. Still a probability, not a certainty.
